explain.narrative:
## BufferedReader and BufferedWriter

BufferedReader.readLine returns null at end of input. BufferedWriter accumulates characters and offers newLine for a platform line separator. Closing a wrapper closes its underlying stream.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var reader = new java.io.BufferedReader(new java.io.StringReader("first\nsecond"))) { System.out.println(reader.readLine()); } } }
examples.explanation: Reads one complete line with BufferedReader.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter(); var buffered = new java.io.BufferedWriter(writer)) { buffered.write("buffered text"); buffered.flush(); System.out.println(writer); } } }
examples.explanation: Writes buffered characters and flushes them to the underlying writer.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var reader = new java.io.BufferedReader(new java.io.StringReader("a\nb"))) { System.out.println(reader.readLine()); System.out.println(reader.readLine()); System.out.println(reader.readLine()); } } }
examples.explanation: readLine returns null when no more lines remain.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter(); var buffered = new java.io.BufferedWriter(writer)) { buffered.write("A"); buffered.newLine(); buffered.write("B"); buffered.flush(); System.out.println(writer.toString().replace(System.lineSeparator(), "|")); } } }
examples.explanation: Uses newLine to insert the platform-specific line separator.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var reader = new java.io.BufferedReader(new java.io.StringReader("one"))) { System.out.println(reader.readLine() != null); } } }
examples.explanation: Uses a null check to detect whether a line was read.
